dict.string: Managed settings for cmux (every channel). Keys are cmux.json key paths; capitalized keys are policy keys. Forced values lock the setting; non-forced values replace its default. Exception: agents.chats.roots adds locked roots to the user list; agents.chats.enabled and agents.chats.discovery can only be forced off.
The language of cmux's menus, pages and messages.
Lists finished shell commands in History. Command lines can contain secrets.
What Go Back and Go Forward walk.
Everything also steps through tabs and panes inside a workspace.
Each machine deletes recorded commands that are older.
Older closed tabs, workspaces and windows are deleted. 0 keeps them all.
Each machine deletes closed items that are older. 0 keeps them however old they are.
Minimal has no titlebar strip; the top row moves the window.
With the sidebar hidden, On Hover shows its buttons only over the top row.
Show/Hide All Windows (⌃⌥⌘.) works while another app is in front.
⌃⌥⌘Space starts an agent while another app is in front.
cmux stays in the menu bar until a window opens.
Hide Dock Icon When No Windows Are Open
The layout of the New Tab page. Terminal opens a terminal instead.
Cmd-T opens the faster native New Tab page. Recent chats and widgets are web only.
An extension id that draws New Tab, such as "local/showcase-newtab". Unset: cmux's own.
Applies in Minimal Mode; otherwise the + always shows.
Where the address bar of browser and Markdown panes sits.
Whether the tab bar sits above or below the address bar.
The rest are in the More menu.
Text size of tab titles. Unset, tabs follow the interface size.
Height of a pane's tab bar. Its tabs grow and shrink with it.
Shrink narrows tabs before scrolling; Scroll keeps them wide.
Machines shows each shell tab with the icon of the machine it runs on.
Widest a tab gets when the strip has room.
The selected tab stays at least this wide when tabs shrink.
Narrowest the other tabs get before the strip scrolls.
Hold Option to reverse it for one click.
Tabs in a list beside the panes. A tab bar's menu changes one workspace.
Use Vertical Tabs for All Workspaces
Show titles while the pointer is over the collapsed list.
Expand Collapsed Vertical Tabs on Hover
Hide the Tab of a Chat Alone in Its Pane
Cmd-T opens a workspace and Cmd-N opens a tab.
Warn Before Closing a Running Program
Warn Before Closing a Working Agent
Terminals run in cmux-tui and keep running after cmux quits unless you end them.
Ask before Cmd-Q ends agents or terminals.
Ask Before Quitting Ends Agents or Terminals
⌘Q asks before quitting; press it again to quit. The Quit menu item and the Dock quit at once.
A share of the window width, for Fixed Width new columns.
A thin bar under the columns that shows and moves the visible range.
Which pane gets focus when the focused pane closes.
Hold Command or Control for 0.30 seconds to show shortcut hints.
Show Shortcuts When Holding a Modifier
Stable gets builds that ran a week without problems; Canary and Dev get them first.
Off: cmux asks before downloading. It always asks before restarting.
One click on Update downloads, installs and restarts. Terminals and agents keep running.
An Install button for each version listed in What's New.
While downloads wait, a found update shows on Settings and one click downloads it.
Every Merge gets web UI changes minutes after they land.
Lets cmux live start show your checkout's web UI, each saved edit at once.
A downloaded update installs as cmux quits. Terminals keep running.
Installs a downloaded update after cmux has been idle for the time below, never while an agent is working or a message is unsent. Agents keep running.
How long cmux must be idle before Update When Idle installs.
Earlier builds kept so you can roll back. Uses almost no disk until files change.
A sidebar card links to What's New after an update.
A small tip now and then points at a feature an update added.
A nightly installs when you are idle, and never waits longer than this.
How long you must be idle before a nightly installs.
Short cards from the cmux team above Settings, shown when the pointer is over the sidebar.
Off: cmux never asks the network for announcements. The request carries no identifiers.
What agents may do with the apps on this Mac. Denied apps are never used, in any mode.
Apps no agent may use, in any mode: an app ID, an ID prefix ending in *, or name: and the app's name.
Agents on your other machines, signed in to the same account, may use this Mac's apps.
While you use the mouse or keyboard, agents wait before their next click or key press.
Pause When I Use the Mouse or Keyboard
A blue cursor shows wherever an agent clicks or types.
Each agent cursor can carry a tag: the agent's workspace name, or a tag the agent sets. Show it when your pointer is over the cursor, always, or never.
What an agent waits for after each click or key press before it looks again: the screen to stop changing, a fixed 2 seconds, or nothing.
A small live view of the app an agent uses. Click it for Agent Activity.
Agents may open pop-up and context menus of apps in the background to choose an item. Menu bar menus never open in the background.
Advanced. Agents may bring an app to the front and move your pointer when it takes no background input.
Agents can use the free cmux model while signed out. cmux checks this is a real Mac.
Stops idle sleep while an agent works. Closing the lid still sleeps the Mac.
Keep Mac Awake While Agents Work
A build or test running over a minute keeps the Mac awake.
Terminal agents reopen their session after a crash or restart.
Off, cmux won't switch an agent into a mode that skips approvals.
Agents suggest next tasks you can start as child chats.
Suggests your next prompt in grey; Tab takes it. Each one is an extra model call.
Closing the lid still puts the Mac to sleep.
Keep Mac Awake for Your Phone
Stores workspace names, colors and unread counts. No paths, titles or output.
Show This Mac's Workspaces on Your Phone While It's Off
View only, streamed by this Mac while the page is open.
Show Your Cloud Machine's Screen on Your Phone
By machine name: "#RRGGBB" or an accent name, such as red or blue.
ssh:// links from other apps connect to these hosts without asking.
Each new workspace gets its own Cloud machine, and its chats run there.
Current Folder copies your git working copy to the new machine.

Agents, `cmux cloud` in a terminal and scripts create Cloud machines, move chats to Cloud and start sessions there with no card asking you first. Your plan's limits still apply. Only you can change this.
Let Agents Use Cloud Without Asking
Back to Before This Turn restores the machine in seconds. Keeps the newest few.
Save a Checkpoint Before Each Cloud Chat Turn
Agents can start sessions that work in parallel, shown under theirs.
When an agent in a sub-session asks a question, the session that started it can answer, and the answer shows who gave it. Permission requests always wait for you. Off: only you answer.
Let Sessions Answer Their Sub-sessions' Questions
Finished and closed sub-sessions don't count.
More wait their turn. Lowering it never stops running ones.
1 means sub-sessions cannot start their own.
Tells new Claude Code chats how cmux shows plans, side sessions and recaps.
Tells new Codex chats how cmux shows plans, side sessions and recaps.
Gemini, OpenCode and agents you added get the same guidance.
Skills in ~/.config/cmux/skills (a folder with a SKILL.md each) reach every new chat.
New chats can use the servers listed above.
Retries after rate limits, capacity errors or a dropped connection.
0 waits longer after each failed try.
How many times the chat tries again before it stops and waits for you.
When one subscription runs out, a chat moves to another with the same model.
Compacts an idle Claude chat while its cache is warm, so the next message costs less.
Chats using less of their context window than this are left as they are.
Agents start in folders under your project roots, and in repositories owned by your organizations, without asking. Other folders ask first.
Trust My Own Folders Without Asking
Everything inside these folders is trusted. Use full paths or ~/ paths.
A repository is trusted when all of its GitHub remotes belong to these users or organizations.
The cmux app on your iPhone can open this Mac's workspaces, on the same account.
The size of a terminal shown on this Mac and a phone at once.
The devices a shared terminal sizes to first, highest first.
Even gives every pane in the column the same size after a split.
Off hides New Row and fits a column's existing rows into it without scrolling.
Pointing at or scrolling over a pane focuses it.
Panes that do not fit scroll sideways instead of shrinking.
What moves columns and rows: Command + Scroll, or a plain sideways scroll.
Pages like Figma keep Command + Scroll. Off, it always moves columns.
Web Pages Get Command + Scroll First
Split Automatically splits the largest pane.
With Split Automatically, new browsers also get their own pane instead of a tab.
Keeps a chat as the main pane, with what it opens in a column on its right.
An unnamed workspace shows its front tab's name. Your own name always wins.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope.

Commands shown first when the command palette opens, in this order, by action id.
Rows you pick and use often rank higher. Off records nothing.
Show chats stored on this device. Nothing is uploaded.
Find harness chat folders automatically. When off, only the listed folders are used.
A line on where a Claude chat stands when you come back. Each is a small model call.
Unused chats are compressed into one small file each and open as before.
Days unused before a chat is compressed. Busy chats never are.
Archives chats after a period of no activity. Chats that are running or have background work never are.
Where cmux chat starts a chat with no --on: here, cloud, vm:NAME or a device name.
Listed under Locations. Use full or ~/ paths.
Also shows the folders of apps like CleanShot X and Shottr.
Also shows the pictures and videos in these folders.
Archived workspaces stay dimmed in their group and come back when opened.
Days unopened and unchanged. Pinned, running and waiting workspaces never archive.
Archive and remove worktrees agents finished with, and trim the build output of idle ones. Unpushed work is kept in git and comes back when the chat reopens.
Also remove this Mac's build caches nobody used lately, such as Xcode DerivedData. Package caches go only when the disk is nearly full.
Frees the memory of unused workspaces. Terminals and agents keep running.
Minutes a workspace goes unopened and unchanged before it hibernates.
Idle minutes before the workspaces of a space no window shows hibernate.
Ends idle shells of long-unused workspaces; they restart in the same folder.
Minutes before a hibernated workspace's idle shells end (1440 is a day).
Also ends idle Claude Code and Codex sessions; opening the tab resumes them.
What happens to a command that still runs in a workspace that frees its terminals.
Inbox lists what needs you first, with the task beside it. Changes apply at once.
The icon drawings used by cmux.
Colors for terminals. A space, workspace or terminal theme overrides it.
Colors for the window, sidebar, tabs and pages. Terminals use Terminal Theme.
Your color changes to a theme, such as "Rose Pine/background": "#1f1d2e".
Themes starred in a theme picker. The picker lists them first.
Switches the terminal theme to the next starred one. Needs two starred themes.
The color of selection, focus and the Send button.
Accent tints the selected row and tab with the accent. Neutral keeps them gray.
A theme file in ~/.config/cmux/themes, such as "tokyo" for tokyo.json.
Settings you changed while a theme file sets them. Your value applies over the file's; resetting the row returns to the file's. Choosing another theme file clears the list.
The color of selected text everywhere. Unset uses the terminal theme's.
A painting behind the window. Lower Opacity to see it.
A painting, your wallpaper or a macOS wallpaper behind the window.
How often a shuffled background changes. Also accepts a number from 1 to 1440 in a raw profile.
Unset, it shows the dark picture.
Unset, it shows the light picture.
A time (07:00) or sun event (sunset-30m) for each picture.
Follow light and dark, or change with the sun through the day.
Latitude,longitude for sunrise and sunset, such as 37.77,-122.42. Unset: your time zone.
The folder and picture each background mode last showed, so switching back restores them.
Picture ID to fill, fit, center or stretch, with optional X Y anchor and zoom.
The backgrounds shown before, newest first, so one click goes back.
Display ID to daily, folder:<path>, desktop, a background or none.
Display ID to 15m, hourly or daily. Others use the global rotation.
One background behind the window, or a copy in each pane.
The plain theme color, without paintings, wallpapers or glass.
Calm while agents are idle; a soft glow in the machine's color when an agent needs you.
Draws menus, popovers, the composer and cards with the glass from before November 2026.
Applies Hue and Saturation to the window's tint. Off, they have no effect.
How much of the theme color covers the material behind the window.
Unset, the window follows Ghostty's background-opacity and background-blur.
How much windows behind the front one are tinted. 0 keeps them the same.
The glass takes the colors of your desktop picture.
How much of the desktop or wallpaper shows through the glass.
Shift the tint color around the hue wheel.
Increase or reduce the tint color intensity.
Row height, padding, corners, icons and text size together.
Zoom for chat, Settings and other app pages.
Text size of the sidebar, tabs, menus and chat. Terminals have their own size.
How text draws. Some text changes after cmux restarts; terminals keep their own.
Text size of tabs, the sidebar and other controls. Terminal text has its own size.
None removes every border, hairline and separator in the app.
Off draws the composer, menus, popovers and cards as solid surfaces with a plain border.
How the focused pane stands out.
How other panes' tabs look subtler when Focused Pane marks tabs.
Whether panes sit in one rounded card, and where lines are drawn.
The title bar, tab bar and sidebar in the content's color, or shaded apart.
How much darker the title bar, tab bar and sidebar are. 1 is the default.
The sidebar and tab bar in one tone, the panes in another. Works with every window style and theme.
How the selected tab meets the content below it: a pill, flush with it, or flowing into it like a drop of water.
Splits, closes, moves, zooms and column scrolls slide into place.
A new tab grows into its place in the tab bar. Off shows it there at once.
A new workspace row opens in the sidebar. Off shows it there at once.
One radius for panes, tabs, panels, popovers and cards.
Space between a pane's edge and its tabs. Inner corners use the corner radius minus this.
Calm stops sliding, spinning and hover highlights; Still also makes animations instant.
Off turns every animation off. On, the switches below pick by area.
Rows, groups and the sidebar itself slide as they change.
Tabs grow, shrink and slide as they open, close and move.
Splits, closes, zooms, dividers and windows move with motion.
Menus, popovers, the palette, sheets, toasts and cards fade and slide.
Hover cards and tooltips fade and slide in. Off: they show and hide at once.
The Chief chat, its bubbles, the composer and the Home list move and fade.
The agent cursor glides and shows click ripples.
Spinners turn, status dots pulse and attention flashes blink.
Hover, press, focus and theme color changes ease in.
Animations in cmux's own pages, such as chats and New Tab. Websites are unchanged.
How sidebar rows, tabs and panes show work in progress.
Static draws a still, distinct shape for each state. Reduce Motion always uses Static.
Three dots take the tab's icon place while an agent works.
A spinner takes a browser tab's icon place while its page loads.
A status that asks for a style (cmux status set --style) uses it.
A shell command that runs a while shows as busy.
Stage All and Revert All Bar
Image sites can see your address and when you open a document.
The widest a line gets, in characters.
Text fills the whole pane instead of the text width.
The size viewers open at. Cmd-= and Cmd-- change one viewer.
The gap after each paragraph, as a share of the text size.
Code size as a share of the text size.
The widest the chat's column gets. On a wider pane the chat stays centered. Also accepts a number from 480 to 4000 in a raw profile.
The chat fills the whole pane instead of the text width.
A small picture of the whole chat at its right edge. Click or drag it to scroll.
Keeps the agent's task list under the latest message, not over the composer.
A soft sound when a long turn ends, its checks pass or its pull request merges.
Hides the running work bar. Hover the top of the composer to bring it back.
Where the running tray's handle sits on top of the composer.
A banner for new turns when you come back to a chat. Right-click it to hide it.
Which is big in a sender's icon: the model's mark or the session badge.
The small colored glyph on a sender's icon that tells sessions of one model family apart.
Where the small glyph sits on a sender's icon.
The font of the whole chat: replies, the composer, cards and menus.
A font family or a comma list of them. When set, it replaces the Chat Interface Font.
The font of the agent's replies. When set, it replaces the Chat Font.
A font file for each family, such as "Lora:italic": "file:~/Fonts/Lora-Italic.woff2".
Empty uses the Markdown viewer's code font.
Code as a share of the chat's text size. Empty uses the Markdown viewer's.

Where the chip sits: under the tabs (Left) or in the header (Right).
What runs down the chat's edge.

Token values that override the transcript look.
After a chat with many corrections, shows a better first prompt.

Comma-separated -ing verbs for the live status line.
How the light band moves across the live status line.
How long one continuous pass of the shimmer takes.

Columns where a vertical line shows.

How the sections above and below the workspace list draw.

The share of the sidebar the bottom sections fill before they scroll.
